en: The Apadāna of the Elder Kaṇaverapupphiya Supāricariyavagga, Chapter 2 I am the Buddha’s disciple, a monk who has attained the goal. Having abandoned birth and death, I have reached the end of suffering. (1) In the past, when the lifespan was twenty thousand years, there appeared in the world the Blessed One Kassapa, the Worthy One, the Perfectly Enlightened One. (2) At that time, I was a merchant’s son living in Benares; having heard of the appearance of the Buddha, I went to the Teacher. (3) There I saw the Teacher, the Blessed One Kassapa, the Worthy One, the Perfectly Enlightened One, endowed with the thirty-two marks of a Great Man.

(4) Seeing him, I was filled with joy and great rapture; I took a kaṇavera flower and offered it to the Buddha. (5) Having made that offering to the Buddha, the Great Sage, I then paid homage at his feet and departed from his presence. (6) Through that root of merit, having passed through many births, I was reborn in heaven and experienced the bliss of the gods. (7) For eighty-four thousand aeons I dwelt in the celestial realms; then, having fallen from there, I was born in the human world. (8) For eighty-four thousand aeons I lived as a king of men; and for eighty-four thousand aeons I was a lord of the gods. (9) For eighty-four thousand aeons I was a wheel-turning monarch; and for eighty-four thousand aeons I was a universal sovereign. (10) For eighty-four thousand aeons I was a wealthy householder; and for eighty-four thousand aeons I was a powerful king. (11) For eighty-four thousand aeons I was a brahmin of great wealth; and for eighty-four thousand aeons I was a learned priest. (12) For eighty-four thousand aeons I was a wealthy merchant; and for eighty-four thousand aeons I was a prosperous trader. (13) For eighty-four thousand aeons I was a wealthy farmer; and for eighty-four thousand aeons I was a master of the fields. (14) For eighty-four thousand aeons I was a wealthy artisan; and for eighty-four thousand aeons I was a skilled craftsman. (15) For eighty-four thousand aeons I was a wealthy physician; and for eighty-four thousand aeons I was a master of healing. (16) For eighty-four thousand aeons I was a wealthy caravan leader; and for eighty-four thousand aeons I was a merchant chief. (17) For eighty-four thousand aeons I was a wealthy guildmaster; and for eighty-four thousand aeons I was a leader of the assembly. (18) For eighty-four thousand aeons I was a wealthy village headman; and for eighty-four thousand aeons I was a lord of the district. (19) For eighty-four thousand aeons I was a wealthy town guard; and for eighty-four thousand aeons I was a protector of the city. (20) For eighty-four thousand aeons I was a wealthy gatekeeper; and for eighty-four thousand aeons I was a guardian of the gates. (21) For eighty-four thousand aeons I was a wealthy watchman; and for eighty-four thousand aeons I was a sentinel. (22) For eighty-four thousand aeons I was a wealthy messenger; and for eighty-four thousand aeons I was a bearer of news. (23) For eighty-four thousand aeons I was a wealthy servant; and for eighty-four thousand aeons I was an attendant. (24) For eighty-four thousand aeons I was a wealthy slave; and for eighty-four thousand aeons I was a laborer. (25) For eighty-four thousand aeons I was a wealthy cook; and for eighty-four thousand aeons I was a preparer of food. (26) For eighty-four thousand aeons I was a wealthy baker; and for eighty-four thousand aeons I was a maker of cakes. (27) For eighty-four thousand aeons I was a wealthy brewer; and for eighty-four thousand aeons I was a maker of drinks. (28) For eighty-four thousand aeons I was a wealthy florist; and for eighty-four thousand aeons I was a gardener. (29) For eighty-four thousand aeons I was a wealthy garland-maker; and for eighty-four thousand aeons I was a wreath-weaver. (30) For eighty-four thousand aeons I was a wealthy perfumer; and for eighty-four thousand aeons I was a maker of scents. (31) For eighty-four thousand aeons I was a wealthy dyer; and for eighty-four thousand aeons I was a colorist. (32) For eighty-four thousand aeons I was a wealthy weaver; and for eighty-four thousand aeons I was a cloth-maker. (33) For eighty-four thousand aeons I was a wealthy tailor; and for eighty-four thousand aeons I was a seamstress. (34) For eighty-four thousand aeons I was a wealthy smith; and for eighty-four thousand aeons I was a metalworker. (35) For eighty-four thousand aeons I was a wealthy carpenter; and for eighty-four thousand aeons I was a builder. (36) For eighty-four thousand aeons I was a wealthy mason; and for eighty-four thousand aeons I was a stonemason. (37) For eighty-four thousand aeons I was a wealthy painter; and for eighty-four thousand aeons I was a decorator. (38) For eighty-four thousand aeons I was a wealthy scribe; and for eighty-four thousand aeons I was a clerk. (39) For eighty-four thousand aeons I was a wealthy accountant; and for eighty-four thousand aeons I was a calculator. (40) For eighty-four thousand aeons I was a wealthy astrologer; and for eighty-four thousand aeons I was a reader of omens. (41) For eighty-four thousand aeons I was a wealthy physician; and for eighty-four thousand aeons I was a healer. (42) For eighty-four thousand aeons I was a wealthy teacher; and for eighty-four thousand aeons I was a preceptor. (43) For eighty-four thousand aeons I was a wealthy student; and for eighty-four thousand aeons I was a scholar. (44) For eighty-four thousand aeons I was a wealthy ascetic; and for eighty-four thousand aeons I was a forest-dweller. (45) For eighty-four thousand aeons I was a wealthy hermit; and for eighty-four thousand aeons I was a practitioner of austerities. (46) For eighty-four thousand aeons I was a wealthy yogin; and for eighty-four thousand aeons I was a meditator. (47) For eighty-four thousand aeons I was a wealthy sage; and for eighty-four thousand aeons I was a seer. (48) For eighty-four thousand aeons I was a wealthy recluse; and for eighty-four thousand aeons I was a renunciant. (49) For eighty-four thousand aeons I was a wealthy monk; and for eighty-four thousand aeons I was a bhikkhu. (50) For eighty-four thousand aeons I was a wealthy lay follower;

and for eighty-four thousand aeons I was a devotee. (51) For eighty-four thousand aeons I was a wealthy upāsaka; and for eighty-four thousand aeons I was a faithful one. “The Blessed One named Siddhattha,
the eldest in the world, the bull among men,
was preceded by his disciples.”
Enter the city.
I was in the king’s inner palace,
appointed as the trusted guardian.
Seated in my palace,
I beheld the Leader of the World.
Having taken a kaṇavera flower, I offered it to him.
I scattered it over the Saṅgha of bhikkhus;
having set aside a portion for the Buddha,
I scattered even more than that.
For ninety-four eons,
because I offered that flower in worship,
I have not known a state of misery.
This is the fruit of worshipping the Buddha.
Eighty-seven aeons hence,
four [of us] shall possess great supernormal power.
Possessing the seven treasures,
they are wheel-turning monarchs of great power.
The four analytical knowledges—
the Buddha's teaching has been accomplished.
Thus indeed did the Venerable Elder Kaṇaverapupphiya speak these verses.
The legend of the elder Kaṇaverapupphiya is the second.
